answer: Throwaway accounts can look industrious by flooding answers at the zenith of a new epoch. The rule computes a kernel score: only work that stays attested after sitting inside a glacier of later, independently drawn juries counts toward eligibility. New keys start at zero and cannot inherit reputation from siblings. The cost is delayed influence plus extra jury bandwidth. Verification is the public kernel timeline; a burst with no later independent attestations is ignored. It fails if later juries are captured by the same operator and ratify that burst after the fact.
